docs.title: Python Package Template
docs.text: A Python library template with uv, Pydantic settings, loguru, pytest, Ruff, Git hooks, generated API docs and Conventional Commit releases. Supports Python 3.12–3.14.8.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text:
With Make, Bash, Git and uv available:

git clone https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/python-package-template.git
cd python-package-template
make install-dev
make pre-commit-install
make check
make run

This installs the editable package and tools, sets up hooks, validates the checkout and runs the example. No live service or integration credentials are required. make help lists all commands.

docs.title: Use the package
docs.text:
Download a wheel from this repository's GitHub Releases, then install that file:

uv pip install "/path/to/python_package_template-<version>-py3-none-any.whl"

from python_package_template.example import hello

hello()

Releases attach a wheel and sdist to GitHub and publish documentation on GitHub Pages; this template does not publish to a package index.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
1. Follow Setup, then coordinate on an issue.
  2. Branch from dev: feature/<name> or bugfix/<name>.
  3. Update the relevant docs and run make check (Testing).
  4. Open a PR to dev using a Conventional Commit title. PRs are squash-merged; the title determines the version.

See Release for publication and recovery. Coding agents need explicit approval for commits, pushes and publishing. Follow the Code of Conduct; report security issues through SECURITY.md, never a public issue.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
We take security issues seriously. We appreciate your efforts to responsibly disclose your findings and will make every effort to acknowledge your contributions.

Please do NOT open a public issue or pull request for security vulnerabilities.

To report a security vulnerability privately, use GitHub private vulnerability reporting (preferred):

  • https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/python-package-template/security/advisories/new

For any other question, open an issue to reach the contributors of this repository, but never include vulnerability details in a public issue.

When reporting, please include as much of the following as possible:

  • A description of the vulnerability and its impact
  • The affected component(s) and version(s)
  • Steps to reproduce the issue
  • Any suggested remediation (if known)

You should receive a response within 48 hours. If you do not, please follow up on the same channel.

docs.title: Supported Versions
docs.text: Security updates are only provided for the latest released version. Please always use the latest version available.

docs.title: Disclosure Policy
docs.text:
• You will receive an acknowledgment of your report within 48 hours.
  • We will investigate the issue and determine its impact and severity.
  • We will fix the issue in a future release and credit you if you wish to be credited.
  • We ask that you do not publicly disclose the vulnerability until we have published a fix and given users time to update.

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep everything up to date.
  • Do not expose admin interfaces directly to the internet without a reverse proxy and proper authentication.
  • Use strong, unique passwords and enable multi-factor authentication where available.

docs.title: 1. Setup
docs.text: Prepare the package, development tools and documentation environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Make, Bash, Git and uv on Linux, macOS or Windows with Git Bash/WSL. uv provisions Python 3.12–3.14.8; run make install-uv if uv is missing.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/python-package-template.git
cd python-package-template
make install-dev
make pre-commit-install
make check
make run

This creates .venv, installs the editable package and Git hooks, validates the checkout and runs the greeting example. No integration service or credentials are needed. Optionally copy .env.example to .env to customize settings such as LOGGING_LEVEL.

docs.title: Optional environments
docs.text:
Command Use make install-tools Static/docs tools without the application dependencies make install-release Packaging and release tools make docker-build Build the development image make docker-dev Open a container with this project mounted in /app make docker-prod Open a shell in the built image

Inside the container, use make run and make check. If a mounted host .venv conflicts, recreate it for the container. A manually managed environment can use uv pip install -e .; that alone does not install the development tools.

docs.title: Documentation and editor
docs.text:
make deploy-doc-local

Use .venv/bin/python as the interpreter; mark src and tests as source/test roots. Follow .editorconfig for indentation and line endings. Hooks are installed once with make pre-commit-install; docs/check targets do not reinstall them.

For workflow debugging, Docker plus make install-act enables make act. For publication, see release credentials. Next: Conventions and Testing. make help lists all targets.

Agent rules live in AGENTS.md; CLAUDE.md links to it for Claude Code. Edit AGENTS.md to update the shared instructions.

docs.title: 2. Project structure
docs.text: Where things are, and where to add yours.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
src/python_package_template/
  example.py            example module, console script `hello`
  settings.py           ApplicationSettings (pydantic-settings) and the loguru logger
tests/
  README.md             test map and commands
  unit/                 self-contained package tests
    docs/               API reference generation
    release/            artifacts, release guards and upload recovery
docs/
  developer/            this guide
  examples/             example scripts, rendered as pages by scripts/gen_example_pages.py
  images/               logo and screenshots
scripts/
  emoji_commit_parser.py  semantic-release parser that accepts a leading emoji
  gen_doc_stubs.py        API reference pages from package/workspace source directories
  release_artifacts.py    Git release tags and complete wheel/sdist checks
  gen_example_pages.py    pages from docs/examples/*.py
makefiles/              one .mk per concern, included by Makefile
.github/                workflows, composite actions, Renovate, issue and PR templates
Dockerfile              development / production container
properdocs.yml          documentation site (MkDocs Material)
CHANGELOG.md            written by semantic-release, never by hand

docs.title: Add a module
docs.text:
1. Add src/python_package_template/<module>.py, with Google-style docstrings: they become the API reference page automatically.
  2. Add tests/unit/test_<module>.py, or use a responsibility subfolder for tooling tests.
  3. Log with the package logger: from python_package_template.settings import logger.

docs.title: Add a setting
docs.text:
1. Add a field to ApplicationSettings in settings.py:

    EXAMPLE_ENDPOINT: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="the endpoint")
EXAMPLE_API_KEY: Optional[SecretStr] = Field(default=None, description="the api key")

  2. Set it by environment variable or .env; add it, empty or with a safe default, to .env.example.

  3. Secrets are SecretStr: read them with .get_secret_value(); they print as **********.

docs.title: Add an example
docs.text: Drop a .py file in docs/examples/. Its module docstring becomes the description on the Examples page.

docs.title: 3. Conventions
docs.text: The rules every change follows.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Use the make targets (make help): CI runs the same ones.
  • Docstrings on public functions and classes (Google style): they generate the API reference.
  • Settings through ApplicationSettings (settings.py), not os.environ scattered in the code.

  • Logging with the package's loguru logger, not print:

    from python_package_template.settings import logger

logger.info("Loaded {} items", count)

  • Log, then raise; do not swallow exceptions:

    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
    logger.error(f"File not found: {file_path}. Current directory: {os.getcwd()}")
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"The file {file_path} does not exist.")

In an except block, logger.exception(...) logs the message and the stack trace. Not raising is fine only when the loop must go on.

  • Large data: Polars. CPU-bound work: multiprocessing.Pool.map.

docs.title: Branches and pull requests
docs.text:
1. Branch off dev: feature/<name> or bugfix/<name>. Comment on (or create) the issue first.
  2. Keep up with dev: git merge dev if the branch is pushed, git rebase dev if it is not.
  3. Open a pull request to dev. Its title follows the commit convention below: it becomes the squash commit and decides the version.
  4. When dev is ready, a pull request dev → main releases it.
  5. After a release on main, merge main back into dev (see 5. Release).
Merge Strategy Why feature/* → dev squash one conventional commit per feature dev → main squash one commit for semantic-release to evaluate main → dev (sync) merge commit, direct push squash only applies to pull requests

Never edit project.version or create a tag by hand: semantic-release does both.

docs.title: Commit convention
docs.text:
[emoji] <type>[(<scope>)][!]: <description>, the emoji is optional (Gitmoji).

Emoji Type Aliases Release 🐛 fix bugfix, hotfix patch ⚡️ perf patch ✨ feat feature minor 💥 feat! BREAKING CHANGE: footer major ♻️ 📝 🎨 🧪 🔧 👷 📦 refactor, docs, style, test, chore, ci, build none

On dev, a releasable commit bumps the release candidate instead (1.1.0-rc.1 → 1.1.0-rc.2).

✨ feat(auth): add GitHub App token rotation
🐛 fix(llm): handle empty response from the API
💥 feat!(api): remove the v1 endpoint

feat(auth): redesign token flow

BREAKING CHANGE: /v1/token removed, use /v2/auth instead

Scopes are optional: github, llm, auth, agent, cache, api, ci, deps...

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
• Never write a credential to a file of the repository, even untracked: use .env (git-ignored).
  • detect-secrets runs as a pre-commit hook. For a line that intentionally references a secret (${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}), add # pragma: allowlist secret. Use the --exclude-files / --exclude-lines arguments in .pre-commit-config.yaml only for recurring, structural false positives; never exclude a whole workflow to silence one line.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Adding, renaming or removing one, in the same change: the setting in settings.py, .env.example, and the workflow env: if CI needs it.

docs.title: Renovate
docs.text:
Renovate (.github/renovate.json) opens pull requests for dependencies with a 7-day cooldown; security fixes are not grouped and open at once. PyPI dependencies are ranges in pyproject.toml, locked by uv.lock. Review every Renovate pull request before merging; after merging one, wait for the others to rebase.

  1. Keep requires-python at >=3.12,<=3.14.8 in every package manifest. Write code compatible with Python 3.12; CI runs make test-all on Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14.
  2. Renovate widens the Python upper bound while preserving the 3.12 minimum. Python Docker updates share the runtime update group; review the resulting supported range before merging.
  3. PyPI updates use strict Python compatibility filtering. Weekly lockfile maintenance refreshes versions already permitted by dependency ranges; review the lockfile and CI results too.
  4. Renovate updates dependency files, GitHub Actions and pre-commit revisions; update README and developer documentation when the supported Python range changes. Docs are not rewritten automatically.
  5. Renovate tracks the Node pin used by pre-commit. Stable updates wait seven days and use chore; major LTS upgrades require dependency dashboard approval.

docs.title: 4. Testing
docs.text: Run all existing software tests and static/documentation checks.

docs.title: Before a pull request
docs.text:
After setup, run:

make check

This runs make pre-commit (including strict docs), then make test-all. All current tests are self-contained; there is no integration suite or coverage instrumentation yet. Future integration suites must join test-all and CI.

docs.title: Focused checks
docs.text:
Command Scope make test-all Every existing software test; required comprehensive software check make test-unit / make test-local Unit tests; use ARGS to select cases make test-installation Build the wheel, install it in a throwaway env, load hello make pre-commit Static hooks and strict docs make docs-build Strict docs build only make build-package Build and verify the wheel/sdist separately

For example:

make test-unit N=1 ARGS="-k release"

Tests use four workers by default (N=4). test-all rejects selection filters; empty collections fail. make test-installation (alias make test-smoke-cli) builds the wheel and loads its entry point in an isolated environment; it is not part of test-all.

docs.title: Writing tests
docs.text: Use tests/unit/test_<module>.py; tests/README.md maps docs/release tests. Use tmp_path and monkeypatch so parallel tests share no state or local dotenv settings. Mark async tests with @pytest.mark.asyncio (strict mode). Release tests use isolated Git/GitHub/uv command substitutes and never publish.

docs.title: Hooks and CI
docs.text: Hooks cover syntax/whitespace, Ruff, secrets, the lockfile, Markdown/spelling and strict docs. Commitizen validates messages at commit time; see .pre-commit-config.yaml for details. CI and both release branches run static checks and test-all; summaries include setup failures. Build/package installation checks remain separate, and no live-service validation is claimed.

docs.title: 5. Release
docs.text: Publish Python packages to GitHub Releases and documentation to GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Automatic release
docs.text: Merge a releasable change to dev for a release candidate, or promote dev to main for a stable release. release.yml validates the source, versions and builds every package, then uploads artifacts. A tagged stable release also deploys docs from that tag. Docs-only commits do not publish docs. Versions come from Conventional Commits; never edit versions or create tags manually.

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
Use a clean main (stable) or dev (prerelease), synchronized with origin. Complete setup and GitHub login, then run:

make check
make release

The release command versions, builds and uploads the full wheel/sdist set. It changes Git and GitHub; coding agents need explicit per-action approval. For a stable manual release, publish docs separately from the clean released tag:

make deploy-doc-gh

That command pushes gh-pages and requires separate authorization.

docs.title: Retry an interrupted release
docs.text:
Retry the failed CI job if its tested source still matches the release. Locally, rerun make release on the matching clean release branch. To upload from a clean checkout of the exact release tag:

make build-package
make release-assets

If newer application commits exist, let their own workflow validate/release them. Never rebuild an older release from later source. release-assets can create a missing GitHub release and replaces same-named attachments; it does not publish to a package index.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
gh auth login

Credentials resolve from GH_TOKEN (environment or local .env), then gh login, then a hidden terminal prompt. release-assets uses the token or gh login. CI supplies its automatic GitHub token; never print credentials. A tooling-only environment can use make install-release; docs need make install-tools or make install-dev.

docs.title: Release sequence and safeguards
docs.text:
Target / stage Behavior make release-version Require main/dev, a clean tree and HEAD equal to fetched origin Semantic-release build hook uv lock --upgrade-package "$PACKAGE_NAME" && git add uv.lock && make build-package; build failure stops commit/tag/publication make release-assets Require the tag at HEAD and one wheel/sdist per PACKAGE_PROJECTS entry make release Run versioning, reuse valid artifacts or build missing ones, then upload sequentially

All workspace package versions equal the root version. Tags retain vX.Y.Z-rc.N spelling; Python artifacts use normalized X.Y.ZrcN filenames. CI retries may accept the exact tagged, single-parent chore(release): v<version> [skip ci] child of the tested source; newer application changes require validation. Git hooks are disabled only during semantic-release. With no new version or matching tag at HEAD, make release stops without uploading.

docs.title: Repository settings (once)
docs.text: Enable Actions release write permissions and configure Pages to deploy from gh-pages. Enable squash merging so PR titles determine versions. CI installs frozen tools with install-tools, install-release or install-dev according to the job.

docs.title: After a release: sync main into dev
docs.text: Merge main back into dev after a stable release. Use the stable version/changelog as the base for the next candidate; see branch conventions.

docs.title: 6. Fork this template
docs.text: Start a new Python package from this repository.

docs.title: Rename
docs.text:
What Where distribution name, description pyproject.toml: [project] name, description package folder src/python_package_template/, imports in tests/ and docs/examples/ console script pyproject.toml: [project.scripts] (hello) logger name settings.py: the name used to bind and filter the loguru logger Docker image name makefiles/docker.mk: CONTAINER_NAME documentation README.md, CLAUDE.md, properdocs.yml (site_name, site_author), SECURITY.md, docs/ version and changelog reset project.version to 0.1.0, empty CHANGELOG.md

Then: uv lock, make test-all, make pre-commit.

docs.title: Once on GitHub
docs.text:
1. Create main and dev, and protect them (pull requests only, squash merge).
  2. Workflow permissions "Read and write", and GitHub Pages from gh-pages (5. Release).
  3. Install the Renovate app on the repository.

docs.title: Stay in sync with the template
docs.text:
Shared files: makefiles/, Makefile, scripts/emoji_commit_parser.py, .pre-commit-config.yaml, .markdownlint-cli2.yaml, .github/, docs/developer/.

git remote add template-upstream https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/python-package-template.git
git fetch template-upstream
git checkout template-upstream/main -- makefiles/release.mk   # the files you want
git diff --staged                                              # review before committing

docs.title: ApplicationSettings
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSettings

Configuration for python-package-template.

Values are read from environment variables and optionally overridden by a .env file.

Source code in src/python_package_template/settings.py 
class ApplicationSettings(BaseSettings):
    """Configuration for python-package-template.

    Values are read from environment variables and optionally
    overridden by a ``.env`` file.
    """

    # if .env is present, it will override the environment variables
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", extra="ignore")

    # use .get_secret_value() to get the value
    EXAMPLE_API_KEY: Optional[SecretStr] = Field(default=None, description="the api key")
    EXAMPLE_ENDPOINT: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="the endpoint")

    logging_level: str = Field(
        default="DEBUG",
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("LOGGING_LEVEL", "logging_level"),
        description="Log level (TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL)",
    )

    def model_post_init(self, __context):
        """Called after model initialization."""
        pass

docs.title: Test map
docs.text: Locate self-contained tests and run the existing validation commands.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
tests/unit/
├── test_example.py                 Greeting emitted by the example
├── test_settings.py                Settings defaults, environment overrides and logging
├── docs/test_doc_stubs.py           API references for packages and workspaces
└── release/
    ├── test_artifacts.py           Complete wheel/sdist sets and version spelling
    ├── test_release_guards.py      Preconditions, failed commands and recovery
    ├── test_release_assets.py      Upload prerequisites and build ordering
    ├── conftest.py                 Temporary projects and command setup
    └── fixtures/release_command.py Fake Git, uv, GitHub and Make boundaries

docs.title: Run checks
docs.text:
1. Prepare the locked development tools with make install-dev.
  2. Run make test-all for every existing software test, using four pytest workers by default.
  3. Run make pre-commit for static hooks and strict docs, or make check for hooks and software tests.
  4. Use make docs-build independently when checking documentation.
  5. Run make build-package separately when artifact inputs change; synthetic test artifacts do not prove a real wheel installs or runs.

make test-unit ARGS="-k release" selects a focused diagnostic run. make test-all rejects filters. Release tests execute isolated command substitutes; they never publish or mutate this checkout. Package tests import settings from temporary working directories and do not load local credentials.

There is no integration suite yet. Add tests/integration/ and include its real tests in make test-all when one exists. Report coverage and artifact/runtime checks separately; coverage instrumentation is not currently configured. See the testing guide.
